policy: Nothing here is applied silently: tools/build_webkit_jsc.py verifies the SHA-256 of each file before the patch (or accepts the recorded result), applies it, verifies the result, and records it in the configure fingerprint. Add an entry only with a reason and a removal condition (docs/crtweb_porting.md).

patches.reason: WTF::RawHex gives int64_t/uint64_t their own constructors only for CPU(ADDRESS32) or OS(DARWIN); elsewhere it assumes int64_t is intptr_t (true for Linux/Bionic LP64). CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__), but the compiler's integer types stay Darwin's (int64_t is long long, intptr_t is long): clang's own arm_acle.h/arm_neon.h and builtins require uint64_t == __UINT64_TYPE__, so the typedef cannot be changed (tried: clang crashed). RawHex(uint64_t) was therefore ambiguous in JavaScriptCore/tools/Integrity.cpp. The patch adds one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_INT64_IS_LONG_LONG which the harness passes on macOS.
patches.remove_when: WebKit selects the int64_t overloads by type identity (std::is_same_v<int64_t, intptr_t>) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS to WTF as OS(DARWIN) without pulling in Apple SDK code.

patches.reason: JavaScriptCore's inline assembler for the offlineasm LLInt and its thunks takes the assembler syntax from OS(DARWIN): the `_` symbol prefix (SYMBOL_STRING), `.private_extern _x` versus `.hidden x` (HIDE_SYMBOL), the local label prefix `L` versus `.L`, `.alt_entry`, and the absence of `.cfi_startproc` in the global asm blocks. Those are properties of the Mach-O object format, not of the OS, but CRT presents macOS to WebKit as a Linux-shaped platform (no __APPLE__; see 0001), so the ELF spellings were chosen and would not link or assemble. The patch ORs one more condition, selected by -DWTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM which the harness passes on macOS in baseline-jit mode, into those conditionals (the three in WTF/InlineASM.h, the alt-entry and two cfi conditionals in llint/LowLevelInterpreter.cpp, the `#if OS(DARWIN)` guard offlineasm itself writes into LLIntAssembly.h, and the two `#if OS(DARWIN)` guards arm64.rb writes for Mach-O versus ELF relocation specifiers (`@PAGE`/`@GOTPAGE` versus `:lo12:`/`:got:`)). offlineasm also emits ELF `.size`/`.type` debug directives whenever CMake passes --binary-format=ELF, which it does for CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME Linux, so asm.rb additionally skips them when the environment variable WTF_CRT_MACHO_ASM is set (the harness sets it).
patches.remove_when: WebKit keys the assembler syntax on the object format (__MACH__/__ELF__/_WIN32) instead of OS(DARWIN), or CRT presents macOS as OS(DARWIN) without Apple SDK code.
